headline: Choose increasing numbers with room for the suffix
statement: Return every selection of k distinct integers from the range 1 through n. The order of selected numbers and order of answers are irrelevant.
prerequisites: Basic Python lists, loops, and functions
intuition: Choose k different numbers from 1 through n. Always choose the next number after the previous one, so the same set is not repeated in another order. Stop a branch early when there are too few numbers left to fill the remaining positions.
approach: Maintain an increasing path and its next allowed start.
When the path has k values, save a copy.
Try values from start through n-needed+1, recurse with value+1, then pop.
correctness: Increasing choices ensure every path contains k distinct allowed values. Any k-element subset has exactly one increasing ordering, which is visited. The upper bound prunes only starts lacking enough remaining numbers, so it cannot remove a valid completion.
bruteForce: List all 2^n subsets and retain those of size k. This explores many irrelevant sizes.

complexity.explanation: There are C(n,k) answers, each containing k values, so copying output alone costs O(k*C(n,k)). At n=20,k=10 there are 184756 answers. The working path and recursion stack use only O(k) additional storage; storing the required output is separate.

pitfalls: Recurse with value+1 to prohibit reuse.
Include the upper range endpoint using +1 in Python range.
Do not return the shared mutable path.
